items.title: SAP B1 FP2602 - factur-x.xml overwrite issue
items.author: Johannes_Sippl
items.text:
We are using SAP Business One 10.0 FP2602 on SQL Server and have implemented ZUGFeRD / Factur-X EN16931 using the "PDF with XML Attachment" electronic document protocol. 

 The Factur-X XML itself is generated correctly and the PDF can also be generated with the XML embedded. 

 The problem is the XML file name and the external XML storage. 

 For a valid Factur-X / ZUGFeRD PDF, the embedded XML attachment needs to remain named: 
 factur-x.xml 

 In our current configuration, the same file name is also used for the externally generated XML file in the configured XML folder. 
 So we currently get: 
 ...\XML\factur-x.xml 
 for every invoice. 

 This is a serious problem for us because we have four locations/users that can create invoices at the same time. If several invoices are generated concurrently, all of them potentially write to the same physical file path and file name. 
 We therefore need a unique external path per invoice, while keeping the embedded attachment name inside the PDF as factur-x.xml. 
 The desired result would be something like: 
 ...\XML\260053\factur-x.xml 
 ...\XML\260054\factur-x.xml 
 ...\XML\260055\factur-x.xml 

 while the embedded attachment in each PDF still remains: 
 factur-x.xml 

 According to the SAP Business One documentation, the field "File Name and Path" in the Electronic Documents Export Setup should support dynamic values / data source parameters and subfolders. 
 We therefore tested several variants in a test database. 
 We first tried: 
 [%OINV.DocNum]\factur-x.xml 
 but SAP created a literal folder named: 
 [%OINV.DocNum] 
 We then tried: 
 [%ODOC.DocNum]\factur-x.xml 
 but SAP again created a literal folder named: 
 [%ODOC.DocNum] 
 We also configured a User Query Category for the electronic document protocol. 
 As a test, we created the following query: 
 SELECT T0."DocNum" 
 FROM OINV T0 
 WHERE T0."DocEntry" = [%ODOC.DocEntry] 
 We also tried variants using [%ODOC.DocNum]. 
 Depending on the query, either the parameter was still not resolved in the file path, or XML generation failed with: 
 Error - Cannot map all query parameters 
 We also tested using a query result alias such as: 
 SELECT T0."DocNum" AS "ZUGF_DOCNUM" 
 FROM OINV T0 
 WHERE T0."DocEntry" = [%ODOC.DocEntry] 
 and using: 
 [%ZUGF_DOCNUM]\factur-x.xml 
 but this was also treated literally and did not resolve to the invoice number. 
 If we leave the "File Name and Path" field empty, SAP automatically creates a uniquely named XML file such as: 
 RE_260053.xml 
 However, the same file name is then used inside the PDF attachment as well, so the PDF contains: 
 RE_260053.xml 
 instead of: 
 factur-x.xml 
 If we explicitly configure: 
 factur-x.xml 
 the PDF attachment name is correct, but all invoices use the same external XML file name. 
 So the issue is specifically that we seem to have only one file name setting controlling both: 
 the physical/external XML file name and the embedded XML attachment name inside the PDF 
 We need these two behaviors to be separated, or alternatively we need SAP to support a dynamic subfolder while keeping the file itself named factur-x.xml. 

 Has anyone successfully configured this with SAP Business One 10.0 FP2602 and the "PDF with XML Attachment" protocol? 
 Is there a correct syntax for dynamic paths with this protocol, for example: 
 <InvoiceNumber>\factur-x.xml 
 while keeping the attachment name inside the PDF as: 
 factur-x.xml 
 Or is this a known limitation or bug in FP2602? 

 If this has been corrected in a later patch level, SAP Note or hotfix, I would also appreciate the corresponding reference. 

 Thanks in advance.

4.summary: A blog introduction to key-based partitioning for JMS queues in SAP Cloud Integration. key_points: Single exclusive JMS queue gives global ordering but caps throughput at one consumer.
Most ordering requirements are per business key (for example per order or per customer), not global.
Partitioning by key lets different keys run in parallel while messages with the same key stay in order.
The author claims this works on standard JMS in SAP Cloud Integration without premium add-ons.

The set-cookie value is sent back as a raw Cookie header. Set-Cookie strings carry attributes (Path, HttpOnly, Secure, Expires) that are not valid in a Cookie header, so the cookie name=value pairs need to be extracted.
The session has to be preserved end to end: the token is tied to the server session, so the cookies from the GET must reach the POST.
No solution is given in the thread.

Groovy copies headers.get("set-cookie") as-is. If CPI returns multiple Set-Cookie values as a list, this would send the wrong value.

digest.headline: A thin day: community questions on extracting standard ALV data, ADT refactoring limits and CPI CSRF handling matter more than the mostly truncated blog posts.
digest.overview:
Most blog items today were excerpts or teasers: the BAPI_PO_CREATE1 to EML post, the ALV DATA_CHANGED post, the key-based JMS partitioning post and the AI debugging post all lack the implementation. The usable technical content comes from forum questions. Two ask how to read ALV data from FAGLB03 and FAGLL03H through CL_SALV_BS_RUNTIME_INFO. One reports ADT Extract Method refusing code with SUBMIT ... AND RETURN. One is the ATC finding about buffering on customizing tables in ABAP Cloud. The CPI CSRF question appeared three times.

For a trainer, the useful pattern is that these threads have no accepted answers. They work well as debugging labs: SALV runtime info and its limits, session-bound CSRF tokens with correct Cookie headers, and refactoring preconditions. Treat any fix as a hypothesis to test, not as confirmed. The AI posts (ABAP eval harness, knowledge graph) make unverified accuracy and time-saving claims. Their real issue for classes is governance: what code may go to a cloud model.

top_stories.title: Reading ALV data from standard reports via CL_SALV_BS_RUNTIME_INFO fails in two FAGL cases
top_stories.summary: One poster runs SUBMIT fagl_account_balance (FAGLB03) with CL_SALV_BS_RUNTIME_INFO set to data-only and gets DC006 'GUI cannot be reached'. Their range for rbukrs is typed TY_RANGE_RACCT (a SAKNR range), and there is no sy-subrc check after ASSIGN. Another poster, on S/4HANA 2023 FPS01, uses GET_DATA_REF on FAGL_LINE_ITEM_BROWSER (FAGLL03H) but R_DATA returns the layout-side ALV table, not the line items. Neither thread has an answer.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The runtime-info pattern is common but fragile when the standard program builds several ALV instances or still touches the control framework. The code defects in the first post would break it even after the GUI issue is solved.

top_stories.title: CPI to ABAP OData V4: CSRF token invalid on POST although Postman works
top_stories.summary: The same question appears three times. A GET with x-csrf-token: Fetch succeeds. The POST fails with /IWBEP/CM_V4H_RUN/042 (CSRF_Token_Missing). The workaround copies the x-csrf-token and set-cookie headers into properties via Groovy and sends them as headers. The raw Set-Cookie value is sent as the Cookie header, and this is the likely weak point.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The token is bound to the server session, so the POST must carry the session cookies. Set-Cookie attributes (Path, HttpOnly, Expires) are not valid in a Cookie header, so only name=value pairs should be sent. Multiple Set-Cookie values and header-name case may also break the lookup. These are likely causes to test, not confirmed fixes.

top_stories.title: ADT Extract Method refuses code containing SUBMIT ... AND RETURN
top_stories.summary: On Eclipse 2025-09, ADT 3.52.3 and backend 7.58 SP1, Extract Method fails with 'Source contains program flow change by RETURN'. The workaround is to comment out the SUBMIT, refactor, then restore it. Whether a newer version fixes this is unanswered.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It affects refactoring of legacy code that submits reports. The precheck treats RETURN as flow change, which is correct for a real RETURN statement, but is arguably too strict for the AND RETURN addition.

top_stories.title: ABAP Cloud: ATC info 'Buffering Type is initial but Delivery Class is C'
top_stories.summary: Customizing tables in a BTP ABAP environment app trigger this info-level ATC finding. The reader says table buffering annotations are not available in ABAP Cloud and that buffer configuration objects exist only for CDS views. The options raised are an ATC profile change or an exception. No answer is given.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It shows up on every customizing table in cloud projects. Handling it is a governance decision, and the current buffering options should be checked in the documentation for your release.

top_stories.title: Replacing BAPI_PO_CREATE1 with EML on I_PurchaseOrderTP_2
top_stories.summary: A blog teaser describes creating purchase orders with MODIFY ENTITIES against I_PurchaseOrderTP_2 on S/4HANA 2023 and promises four lessons. The excerpt shows none of them and no code.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The BAPI to EML migration is the direction for new development. Read the full post before using it in class.

top_stories.title: AI for ABAP: unverified claims, real governance questions
top_stories.summary: One poster reports eval accuracy gains for ABAP agent harnesses (92.2% to 97.7%, 88.5% to 93.5%) without methodology and asks if cloud models are allowed. A blog claims a ~90% cut in debugging time by exporting a package with ZGCTS_EXPORT and building a knowledge graph with Claude. Neither gives baselines or metrics.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The numbers cannot be judged. The open issue is which custom code may leave the system, and how to measure results (compile success, ATC findings, unit test pass rate).

top_stories.title: Goods issue reversal reason cannot be captured in standard VL09 or EWM
top_stories.summary: VL09 has no reason field. Reversal material documents (602, 688, Y14, Y41) copy the header text from the original GI. The EWM ReverseGoodsIssue action in UI_WHSEOUTBOUNDDELIVERYORDER has no parameters. Reasons can only be entered in VL02N. The planned workaround is a delivery header field, and the post is truncated.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It maps exactly where the standard stops, which is useful for scoping a clean-core extension for audit needs.

deep_dives.title: Capturing standard ALV data with CL_SALV_BS_RUNTIME_INFO, and why it fails
deep_dives.explanation:
The pattern is: call `CL_SALV_BS_RUNTIME_INFO=>set( display = abap_false metadata = abap_false data = abap_true )`, run `SUBMIT report ... AND RETURN`, then call `get_data_ref( IMPORTING r_data = lr_data )` inside a TRY block catching `cx_salv_bs_sc_runtime_info`. The ALV is meant to be intercepted before display and the data table handed back.

It breaks when the report still builds control framework objects. The FAGLB03 poster gets DC006 'GUI cannot be reached' in a background or submitted context, which means the report's path does not fully honour the runtime-info switch. The FAGLL03H poster gets the other failure: the report creates more than one ALV instance, and `R_DATA` references the layout-side table, not the line items. Neither thread has a confirmed fix.

The first post also has plain code defects. The `rbukrs` range is typed `TY_RANGE_RACCT` (a range of SAKNR) where a company code range is needed. `ASSIGN lt_data_ref->* TO <any_table>` lacks a `sy-subrc` check. `CORRESPONDING` into a local structure only works if field names match the ALV output.

For teaching: first fix the types and checks, then inspect `lt_data_ref` in the debugger to see which table you got. If the report cannot be intercepted cleanly, the more robust route is to read the underlying data source (CDS view, function module or tables) instead of scraping the UI. That is a design suggestion, not something the posts confirm.

deep_dives.title: Session-bound CSRF tokens in CPI calls to ABAP OData V4
deep_dives.explanation:
ABAP Gateway ties the CSRF token to the server session. A GET with `x-csrf-token: Fetch` returns the token and session cookies. The POST is only accepted if it sends the token and the cookies from that same session. Postman keeps a cookie jar, so it works. A CPI HTTP adapter call does not carry cookies between steps unless you pass them.

The posted workaround stores `x-csrf-token` and `set-cookie` as properties in Groovy (`message.getHeaders()`, `message.setProperty(...)`), then sets `x-csrf-token` and `Cookie` headers in a Content Modifier. The weak point is passing the raw Set-Cookie value. Set-Cookie includes attributes such as Path, HttpOnly, Secure and Expires. A Cookie request header should contain only `name=value; name2=value2`. If several Set-Cookie headers come back as a list, the code may also pick up only one or a flattened string. Header key case should be checked too.

Things to test, not confirmed by the thread: log the full header map in the Groovy script; build the Cookie string from name=value pairs of every Set-Cookie entry; confirm GET and POST use the same host, path, client and user; reproduce with curl using `-c` and `-b` first. The response shows `sap-usercontext` and `sap-XSRF_<SID>_<client>` cookies, and a session cookie may also be needed. If the error persists, check the Gateway error log on the ABAP side.

deep_dives.title: ADT Extract Method and flow-change preconditions
deep_dives.explanation:
Extract Method in ADT evaluates the selected range through a POST to `/sap/bc/adt/refactorings` with `step=evaluate`. The poster's selection includes `SUBMIT fagl_account_balance ... AND RETURN` and fails with 'Source contains program flow change by RETURN'. Tested on Eclipse 2025-09, ADT 3.52.3, backend 7.58 SP1.

The precondition has a sound basis: a real `RETURN` in extracted code would leave the new method, not the original routine, so behaviour would change. The open question is whether `AND RETURN` in SUBMIT, which only means the calling program resumes afterwards, is being matched as a flow change. The post does not say whether a newer release fixes this, so check ADT and backend release notes.

The workaround from the post works: comment out the SUBMIT, run Extract Method, then restore it manually and call the new method from the right place. For classes, use it to show how refactoring prechecks work and how to isolate such statements into their own method first.

interview_questions.question: An iFlow in Cloud Integration fetches a CSRF token with a GET and the following POST to an ABAP OData V4 service fails with CSRF_Token_Missing. Postman works. How do you analyse it?
interview_questions.answer: The ABAP CSRF token is bound to the server session, so the POST has to run in the same session as the GET. Postman keeps a cookie jar, whereas the CPI HTTP adapter does not carry cookies between steps by default. I would log the response headers from the GET and check every Set-Cookie value. Then I would build a Cookie request header from name=value pairs only, dropping attributes such as Path, HttpOnly and Expires. I would also confirm that host, client and user are identical in both calls and that the Fetch header was sent correctly. I would reproduce with curl and a cookie jar before changing the iFlow. If it still fails, the Gateway error log on the ABAP side shows the cause.

interview_questions.question: You use CL_SALV_BS_RUNTIME_INFO to capture the ALV output of a standard report submitted with AND RETURN. It aborts with a GUI error, or returns the wrong table. What are the possible causes and alternatives?
interview_questions.answer: The runtime-info switch only works if the report honours it. If the report still builds control framework containers, a background run can abort with DC006. Some reports create several ALV instances, so get_data_ref can return a layout-side or auxiliary table instead of the main data. I would debug to see which table is returned, check the SUBMIT selection types (a SAKNR range used for company code is a bug), and check sy-subrc after ASSIGN. CORRESPONDING only maps fields with matching names. If the report cannot be intercepted reliably, the more robust approach is to read the underlying data via a CDS view, a function module or the tables directly, since scraping UI output is fragile.

interview_questions.question: ADT Extract Method refuses a selection containing SUBMIT ... AND RETURN. Why do such preconditions exist, and how do you proceed?
interview_questions.answer: Extract Method must preserve behaviour. If the selected code contains a RETURN, then after extraction the RETURN would leave the new method, not the calling routine, so the program flow would change. ADT therefore blocks the refactoring and reports 'Source contains program flow change by RETURN'. In the reported case the selection contains SUBMIT ... AND RETURN, where AND RETURN only means the caller resumes, so the check may be stricter than needed. I would check the ADT and backend release notes for a fix. Meanwhile, the poster's workaround is to comment out the SUBMIT, run the refactoring and restore it manually. A cleaner alternative is to extract the SUBMIT into its own method by hand first.
